availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Debug your current Claude Code session by reading the session debug log. (bundled)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Parallel exploration of docs, code, config, tests, and specs to identify cruft, then interactive triage with clear action options. (project)

availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.name: compact
availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

availableCommands.name: context
availableCommands.description: Show current context usage

availableCommands.name: init
availableCommands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

availableCommands.name: pr-comments
availableCommands.description: Get comments from a GitHub pull request

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Review a pull request

availableCommands.name: security-review
availableCommands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

availableCommands.name: insights
availableCommands.description: Generate a report analyzing your Claude Code sessions

{
  "name": "@kynetic-ai/spec",
  "version": "0.10.0",
  "description": "Kynetic Spec - Structured specification format for human-AI collaboration",
  "type": "module",
  "workspaces": [
    "packages/*"
  ],
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "bin": {
    "kspec": "./dist/cli/index.js"
  },
  "repository": {
    "type": "git",
    "url": "git+https://github.com/kynetic-ai/kynetic-spec.git"
  },
  "homepage": "https://github.com/kynetic-ai/kynetic-spec#readme",
  "bugs": {
    "url": "https://github.com/kynetic-ai/kynetic-spec/issues"
  },
  "author": "Kynetic AI",
  "scripts": {
    "bootstrap": "node scripts/bootstrap.cjs",
    "build": "tsc && chmod +x dist/cli/index.js && npm run build:daemon && npm run build:web-ui && npm run build:plugin",
    "build:plugin": "node scripts/build-plugin.cjs",
    "build:daemon": "shx rm -rf dist/daemon && shx mkdir -p dist/daemon && shx cp -r packages/daemon/src/* dist/daemon/",
    "build:web-ui": "shx rm -rf dist/web-ui && cd packages/web-ui && npm run build && shx cp -r build ../../dist/web-ui",
    "dev": "tsx src/cli/index.ts",
    "setup:dev": "npm install && npm run build && npm link",
    "prepack": "npm run build:plugin",
    "pretest": "npm run build",
    "test": "vitest run",
    "test:shard1": "vitest run --shard=1/3",
    "test:shard2": "vitest run --shard=2/3",
    "test:shard3": "vitest run --shard=3/3",
    "test:watch": "vitest",
    "lint": "biome check src/",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"
  },
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=18.0.0"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@elysiajs/cors": "^1.1.3",
    "chalk": "^5.3.0",
    "chokidar": "^4.0.3",
    "cli-table3": "^0.6.5",
    "commander": "^12.1.0",
    "diff": "^8.0.3",
    "elysia": "^1.1.31",
    "js-yaml": "^4.1.0",
    "smol-toml": "^1.6.0",
    "ulid": "^2.3.0",
    "yaml": "^2.8.2",
    "zod": "^3.23.8"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@agentclientprotocol/sdk": "^0.14.0",
    "@biomejs/biome": "2.3.11",
    "@tailwindcss/postcss": "^4.1.18",
    "@types/diff": "^7.0.2",
    "@types/js-yaml": "^4.0.9",
    "@types/node": "^20.11.0",
    "autoprefixer": "^10.4.23",
    "clsx": "^2.1.1",
    "postcss": "^8.5.6",
    "shx": "^0.4.0",
    "tailwind-merge": "^3.4.0",
    "tailwind-variants": "^3.2.2",
    "tailwindcss": "^4.1.18",
    "tsx": "^4.7.0",
    "typescript": "^5.3.3",
    "vitest": "^4.0.17"
  },
  "files": [
    "dist",
    "templates",
    "plugin"
  ],
  "keywords": [
    "specification",
    "requirements",
    "yaml",
    "cli",
    "ai",
    "agent"
  ],
  "license": "MIT"
}

## Package Relationship & Schema Import Analysis

Based on my exploration of the codebase, here's the complete picture of how packages relate and how schema types should be imported:

### Project Structure Overview

```

│   ├── index.js/.d.ts          # Main entry point exports
│   ├── daemon/                  # Copied daemon source
│   └── web-ui/                  # Built web-ui
├── packages/
│   ├── shared/                  # Shared types (NO dependencies on zod)
│   │   ├── package.json        # @kynetic-ai/shared
│   │   ├── src/
│   │   │   ├── index.ts        # Re-exports api, websocket, schemas
│   │   │   ├── api.ts          # Pure TypeScript API types
│   │   │   ├── websocket.ts    # Pure TypeScript WebSocket types
│   │   │   └── schemas.ts      # Basic type enums (TaskStatus, etc.)
│   │   └── tsconfig.json       # No path mappings
│   ├── daemon/                 # Kspec daemon server
│   │   ├── package.json        # @kynetic-ai/daemon, depends on @kynetic-ai/shared
│   │   ├── src/
│   │   └── tsconfig.json       # No path mappings
│   └── web-ui/                 # SvelteKit web dashboard
│       ├── package.json        # @kynetic-ai/web-ui, depends on @kynetic-ai/shared
│       ├── src/
│       └── tsconfig.json       # No path mappings
└── tsconfig.json               # Root tsconfig with path mappings (dev-only)
```

### Key Findings

#### 1. **Root `src/` Produces npm Package**
   - The root `src/` is compiled by `tsc` into `dist/`
   - Published as `@kynetic-ai/spec` npm package
   - Contains the CLI, parser, and **Zod schemas**
   - `dist/index.js` exports everything: `export * from "./parser/index.js"; export * from "./schema/index.js";`

#### 2. **Zod Schemas Location & Availability**
   - **Source**: `/src/schema/meta.ts` (and other schema files)
   - **Compiled**: `/dist/schema/meta.d.ts` and `/dist/schema/meta.js`
   - **Exported from root**: `dist/index.d.ts` re-exports all schemas
   - **Example**: `AgentDispatchEventSchema` is a Zod enum defined in `src/schema/meta.ts` line 23-28

#### 3. **Packages/Shared Package** 
   - **Purpose**: Share types between daemon and web-ui
   - **Has NO dependencies on `zod`** (see package.json dependencies)
   - **Contains ONLY pure TypeScript types**, no schemas
   - **Exports**: API types, WebSocket types, and basic type enums
   - **Example exports**:
     - `api.ts`: `TaskSummary`, `TaskDetail`, `ErrorResponse`, etc.
     - `websocket.ts`: `WebSocketCommand`, `WebSocketEvent`, etc.
     - `schemas.ts`: Type enums like `TaskStatus`, `ItemType`, etc.

#### 4. **Workspace Path Mappings** (Development Only)
   - Root `tsconfig.json` has path mappings for dev:
     ```json
     "paths": {
       "@kynetic-ai/shared": ["./packages/shared/src"],
       "@kynetic-ai/daemon": ["./packages/daemon/src"],
       "@kynetic-ai/web-ui": ["./packages/web-ui/src"]
     }
     ```
   - These are **dev-only** for TypeScript resolution during development
   - Individual packages have **no path mappings** in their own tsconfigs

#### 5. **Current Import Patterns**
   - **web-ui imports from shared**:
     ```typescript
     import type {
       TaskSummary, TaskDetail, ItemSummary, ItemDetail,
       InboxItem, SessionContext, PaginatedResponse, ErrorResponse
     } from '@kynetic-ai/shared';
     ```
   - **daemon imports from shared**:
     ```typescript
     import type { PlanSummary } from '@kynetic-ai/shared';
     ```
   - **All import from root parser** (not schema):
     ```typescript
     import { initContext, loadAllItems, ... } from '../../parser/index.js';
     ```

#### 6. **Build & Package Publishing**
   - Root package.json:
     - `"main": "dist/index.js"` → Main entry point
     - `"types": "dist/index.d.ts"` → Type definitions
     - `"bin": { "kspec": "./dist/cli/index.js" }` → CLI binary
     - `"files": ["dist", "templates", "plugin"]` → Published files
   - Build script: `npm run build` → TypeScript compiles root, then copies daemon source, builds web-ui

### Answer to Your Questions

**Q: Can packages/shared import from src/schema/meta.ts directly?**

**A: No.** Here's why:
- `packages/shared` has no `zod` dependency
- `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` has no path mappings
- When `@kynetic-ai/shared` is published, it's just `dist` with built TypeScript types
- Importing `src/schema/meta.ts` would create a dependency on zod at runtime

**Q: How should we handle this?**

**A: Two approaches:**

1. **Duplicated Type Definitions (Current Pattern)**
   - `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts` defines plain TypeScript type enums
   - No zod dependency needed
   - Example: `TaskStatus` = `'pending' | 'in_progress' | ...`
   - This mirrors the root schema enums but without Zod overhead

2. **If You Need Zod Schemas in shared**
   - Add `zod` to `packages/shared/package.json` dependencies
   - Re-export from root: `export * from '@kynetic-ai/spec';`
   - But this adds zod as a transitive dependency for daemon/web-ui

**Q: Where is the build step for root src/?**

**A: In `package.json` scripts:**
```json

"build:daemon": "shx rm -rf dist/daemon && shx mkdir -p dist/daemon && shx cp -r packages/daemon/src/* dist/daemon/",
```

- `tsc` compiles root `src/` → `dist/`
- Daemon source files are copied to `dist/daemon/` (not compiled separately)
- Web-ui is built separately with Vite → `dist/web-ui/`

- `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/src/schema/meta.ts` - Zod schemas with AgentDispatchEventSchema

- `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/tsconfig.json` - Root config with path mappings (dev-only)
- `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/shared/tsconfig.json` - Package config (no mappings)
